summary: Feed s119_double is degraded: IDS receives incomplete bidirectional traffic with 21.5% duplicate packets and 61.9% one-way TCP sessions, preventing full session reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the same packets twice to the IDS - typically from aggregating two SPANs/TAPs that see the same traffic (e.g., upstream + downstream or core aggregation) without deduplication enabled. 330 of 1538 packets (21.5%) exceed 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles processing duplicates, inflates connection state and alerts, can cause false positives and missed true positives due to state table exhaustion and incorrect TCP reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to strip identical packets within a short window before delivery, giving IDS a single clean copy of each packet without overload.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP is delivered to the IDS - 65 of 105 sessions (61.9%) are one-way. IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true). Likely caused by asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN/TAP or broker aggregation/load-balancing that splits client->server and server->client to different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams, track state, or match bidirectional signatures. Results in missed intrusions, broken stream reassembly, and high false-negative rate for an IDS that needs full payload both ways.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port using symmetric hashing, ensuring complete sessions for detection.
